newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, May 24 Initial Claims from 322,000; May 24 Four-Week Average from 327,500; May 17 Continued Claims from 2,288,000 and May 10 from 2,273,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 320,000 in the May 31 week.

Initial claims in the week ended May 31 were the highest since the May 3 week when they reached 348,000. The four-week moving average was at its lowest level since the week ended April 19 when it stood at 321,750, the department said.
The department said four states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended May 24, the latest period for which data are available.
They were Ohio, with 1,903 fewer initial claims, Louisiana with 1,876, Kentucky with 1,849 and Tennessee with 1,425.

Louisiana said it had fewer layoffs in the transportation equipment industry. Tennessee reported fewer layoffs in the lumber, apparel, leather goods, stone/clay/glass, industrial machinery and service industries, and in manufacturing.
Ohio and Kentucky had no comment on claims activity.
Labor said three states reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the May 24 week.
They were Wisconsin, with 1,061 additional claims filings, North Carolina with 1,037 and Georgia with 1,021.

Wisconsin said it had layoffs in construction, trade and service industries, and in manufacturing. North Carolina reported layoffs in the furniture industry, while Georgia said it had layoffs in the manufacturing sector.
